[USER] User watched "Parasite" for the first time today and is still reeling from the experience.  
[USER] User is planning to have a movie marathon with friends soon.  
[PREFERENCE] User is looking for movie recommendations that tackle social class issues in a similar way to "Parasite."  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant recommended the following movies that explore social class issues:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. **Shoplifters** (2018) - Japanese film by Hirokazu Kore-eda about a family of small-time thieves.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. **The Florida Project** (2017) - Follows the lives of a young girl and her friends growing up in poverty near Disney World.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. **The Square** (2017) - Swedish satire directed by Ruben Östlund critiquing the art world and bourgeoisie.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. **The Death of Mr. Lazarescu** (2005) - Romanian film by Cristi Puiu about an elderly man's journey through a bureaucratic healthcare system.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 5. **Burning** (2018) - South Korean film directed by Lee Chang-dong exploring themes of class and identity.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 6. **The Pursuit of Happyness** (2006) - Biographical drama about Chris Gardner, a struggling single father.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 7. **Ken Loach's films** - Noted for socially conscious filmmaking, including **I, Daniel Blake** (2016), **The Wind That Shakes the Barley** (2006), and **My Name Is Joe** (1998).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 8. **The Housemaid** (2010) - South Korean psychological thriller exploring class divisions and power struggles.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 9. **Roma** (2018) - Semi-autobiographical film by Alfonso Cuarón about a domestic worker in Mexico City.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 10. **Capernaum** (2018) - Lebanese drama about a young boy's journey through the slums of Beirut.
